body.statement: At every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\) at which the constrained tangent space \(\mathcal T_P\) is defined on its actual finite support, the constrained efficient influence function is the coordinatewise orthogonal projection \(\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}G_p\), and the constrained efficiency bound is \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=E_P\{\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}(O)\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}(O)^\top\}\). For every \(a\in\mathbb R^9\), \[a^\top\{\Sigma(p)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}a=\|(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})a^\top G_p\|_{L_2(P)}^2.\] Thus the constrained bound is strictly smaller than the saturated bound in direction \(a\) exactly when \(a^\top G_p\notin\mathcal T_P\). On a smooth local stratum with constant tangent rank and nonsingular information for independent score coordinates, the projection is computable from a finite score matrix by weighted least squares, and a regular local likelihood or one-step estimator attains this bound pointwise. These conclusions do not establish uniform constrained efficiency over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}\), which neither imposes the date-\(4\) restriction nor buffers constrained score rank or support changes.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\), and write \(\langle f,h\rangle_P=E_P\{f(O)h(O)\}\).  The active-frontier theorem proves that the causal target equals \(\Phi(p)\) on every constrained parametric submodel through \(P\), while the analytic-gradient theorem gives
\[
 \dot\theta_P[h]=E_P\{G_p(O)h(O)\},\qquad h\in\mathcal T_P.                                  \tag{1}
\]
The tangent space is closed by definition.  Hence its orthogonal projection exists.  Define coordinatewise
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}G_{p,\ell}.
\]
Since \(G_{p,\ell}-\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}\) is orthogonal to \(\mathcal T_P\),
\[
 \dot\theta_{P,\ell}[h]
 =\langle G_{p,\ell},h\rangle_P
 =\langle\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell},h\rangle_P
 \quad(h\in\mathcal T_P).                                  \tag{2}
\]
If another element of \(\mathcal T_P\) represents the same derivative, its difference from \(\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}\) lies in \(\mathcal T_P\) and is orthogonal to it, hence is zero.  This proves the efficient-gradient characterization and the covariance formula for \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\).

Put \(R_\ell=(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})G_{p,\ell}\).  Orthogonality gives
\[
 \Sigma_{\ell k}(p)
 =\langle\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell},\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,k}\rangle_P
  +\langle R_\ell,R_k\rangle_P.                            \tag{3}
\]
Thus, for every \(a\in\mathbb R^9\),
\[
 a^\top\{\Sigma(p)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}a
 =\left\|\sum_{\ell=1}^9a_\ell R_\ell\right\|_{L_2(P)}^2
 =\|(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})a^\top G_p\|_{L_2(P)}^2.        \tag{4}
\]
This proves both positive-semidefinite dominance and the exact strictness criterion.

For the promised computation, enumerate the actual support as \(s=1,\ldots,m_P\), let \(W_P=\operatorname{diag}(p_1,\ldots,p_{m_P})\), and let the columns of a finite matrix \(S_P\) span the score space obtained by differentiating the absorbing support, two-type factorization, common-kernel, and date-\(4\) restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\).  For coordinate \(\ell\), solve
\[
 \min_{\beta\in\mathbb R^{k_P}}
 \sum_{s=1}^{m_P}p_s\{G_{p,\ell}(s)-S_P[s,:]\beta\}^2.     \tag{5}
\]
The normal equations and unique fitted value are
\[
 S_P^\top W_PS_P\beta=S_P^\top W_PG_{p,\ell},
 \qquad
 \psi_{\mathrm{eff},P,\ell}
 =S_P(S_P^\top W_PS_P)^\dagger S_P^\top W_PG_{p,\ell}.     \tag{6}
\]
The Moore--Penrose inverse makes the fitted value invariant to redundant score generators.

On a smooth local stratum of constant tangent rank, choose independent score coordinates \(\zeta\) for which \(I_P=S_P^\top W_PS_P\) is nonsingular.  The local likelihood score expansion is
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\zeta-\zeta)
 =I_P^{-1}n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nS_P[O_i,:]^\top+o_P(1).       \tag{7}
\]
Equation (1) gives the target derivative
\[
 \dot\theta_{\ell,\zeta}=G_{p,\ell}^\top W_PS_P.           \tag{8}
\]
Combining (7)--(8) produces exactly (6), so the corresponding local likelihood estimator, or its one-step equivalent, attains \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\) pointwise on that stratum.

The broad class \(\mathcal P_\kappa\) buffers the four-slice recovery and saturated marginal variances, but it neither imposes the date-\(4\) common-kernel restriction nor bounds the positive singular values of the constrained score information away from zero.  It also permits support and tangent-rank changes.  Therefore (1)--(8) do not imply uniform constrained efficiency over \(\mathcal P_\kappa\), and no such conclusion is asserted.
body.justification: The projection result identifies potential pointwise efficiency gains only where the fifth-date constrained likelihood has stable local geometry.
body.gap: The headline broad class neither imposes date-4 common kernels nor buffers constrained tangent rank.
body.consumer: A fully specified fifth-date likelihood can use the weighted projection, while the broad guarded bands remain the honest fallback.
